chunks: "If you do good, you will do so for your own good; if you do ill, you will do it for your own loss." So, when the time of the second prediction comes, (We shall rouse another people) to shame you, and enter the Temple as they had done the first time, and to destroy what they conquered utterly.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the second prediction of conquest in Surah Al-Isra?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse establishes the principle of *al-Hasanah bi al-Hasanah* (good for good) and *al-Sayyiah bi al-Sayyiah* (evil for evil), emphasizing that the primary beneficiary or sufferer of one's actions is the self. It is widely interpreted as a prophecy regarding the desecration of the Al-Aqsa Mosque, with many scholars linking the 'second conquest' to historical events such as the Crusades or the eventual return of the enemies to Jerusalem. The verse underscores the cosmic justice where human deeds directly shape their own spiritual and historical destiny.
